tagline.text: An emerald natural swimming pool hidden in a limestone cave on Bantayan Island

location.label: Location
location.text: Inside Ogtong Cave Resort, Barangay Pooc, Santa Fe, Bantayan Island, Cebu

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱200–700 (entrance fee plus getting around the island, per person)

children.text: Ogtong Cave is a small limestone cave inside a privately owned resort in Santa Fe on Bantayan Island, with a turquoise pool of water on its floor. It is close to the port and easy to add to an island tour, and the entrance fee also covers the resort's beach and swimming pool.

Ogtong Cave lies in Barangay Pooc in the Santa Fe area at the southern end of Bantayan Island, which floats in the sea north of Cebu. The cave sits on the private grounds of Ogtong Cave Resort, so it is not a place you walk into from the roadside; it is a paid attraction where you pay the entrance fee at the resort gate. It is about
10 minutes

by road from Santa Fe Port, which makes it an easy stop on your first day on the island or on the day you leave. The resort and the cave share a name, so searching for Ogtong Cave or Ogtong Cave Resort in a map app brings up the same place.
The cave itself is not large. According to visitor guides it runs about

inside, and light seeping in through gaps in the rock keeps it cool but not dark. The floor holds a pool that looks turquoise, and some accounts describe the water as a mix of fresh and sea water whose level changes with the tides. Think of it as a small natural swimming pool underground rather than a giant stalactite cavern, and you will be less likely to feel let down.

From the entrance you go down a short flight of slippery stone steps to the water. In the shallow parts you can stand or sit, and many families with children visit, but kids must be watched by an adult, and some notices say younger children may be restricted from the cave pool. The entrance fee includes the resort's beach and swimming pool, so many visitors plan to stay an hour or two rather than just peek at the cave and leave.

Bantayan Island is best known for its white-sand beaches, island tours and hopping to nearby islets, and Ogtong Cave is one of its few geological attractions. As a result it can get crowded during the day, and one reviewer who arrived around

at lunchtime still found it busy and had to wait for a gap to take photos. For quieter photos, aim for just after opening or late in the afternoon, and plan it as a light stop between beach time. The resort is privately owned, so how it operates can change. As of an April 2026 listing, the beach is open until

You can see the colour of the water from the cave mouth, and as you climb down you find clear turquoise water pooled inside. Light coming in through the rock lights the water, so the cave does not feel dark.

The water is shallow, so you can wear swimwear and get in for a dip. The cave is cooler than outside, which is welcome in the midday heat. The steps are slippery, so wear non-slip footwear or step carefully barefoot.
The entrance fee includes use of the resort's beach and swimming pool. There is also a shallow children's pool, which makes it easy for families to spend half a day.
The resort has a restaurant for lunch or an early dinner, and in-room massage is available by reservation. Opening hours can change with the season, so ask before you visit.

blocks.title: First stop on an island tour

children.text: Because it is close to Santa Fe Port, it often features on motorbike or tricycle island tours. It is a convenient place to visit right after you arrive and drop your bags at your accommodation.
Guests staying at the resort get the cave for free, and guests of Santa Fe Beach Club, run by the same owner, are reported to get free day use. Conditions can change, so confirm when you book.

items.title: Day trip
items.subtitle: From the port to the cave

children.text: Arrive at Santa Fe Port, pay the
environmental fee and complete arrival formalities.
Take a tricycle or motorbike to Ogtong Cave Resort in Pooc. The resort sign is easy to spot along the way.
Pay the entrance fee, go down into the cave and see the pool. The morning is best for photos because there are fewer visitors.
Relax at the resort beach and swimming pool, which are included in the entrance fee.
Have lunch at the resort restaurant or a nearby restaurant.
Head back to Hagnaya or to your accommodation. Check the last boat time in advance.
Guides give different closing times for the cave, at 4, 5 or 6 PM, so confirm on site. We recommend arriving before 3 PM.
Leave your accommodation by motorbike or tricycle and head toward Santa Fe at the south of the island.
See Ogtong Cave and rest for a while at the pool.
After lunch, move on to a beach on the island for a sea swim.
Watch the sunset from the beach and return to your accommodation.
Tricycle tour prices are usually settled by bargaining. Tell the driver where you want to go beforehand to make the fare easier to agree. Some reviewers say the ride to the cave takes around
20 minutes
by motorbike on an island tour, so allow generous travel time.
There are several direct flights a day from Manila (NAIA) to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB), and the flight takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
From the airport to the Cebu North Bus Terminal, take a taxi or Grab; the travel time depends on traffic.
Airfares and airport transfer costs vary a lot by date, so check locally.

Inside the cave you are less affected by the weather, but the boat to the island and the island tour depend on it, so it is best to go in the dry season when the sea is calm.
The cave gets crowded around midday. Going right after opening or late in the afternoon makes it easier to take photos at the water.

From June to November, the rainy season, crossings can be rough or cancelled, and some guides note that jellyfish increase from May to September. On the other hand, rooms are cheaper and it is quieter, so it is not a bad choice if you can adjust your plans to the forecast.

Ogtong Cave Resort has rooms, so you can stay overnight. A 2023 listing shows a twin row house at ₱2,700 and an April 2026 listing about ₱2,800 (a 2011 listing said ₱3,200), with sea-view villas and suites costing more. Taxes are extra and rates vary by season, so confirm when booking. Overnight guests enter the cave for free. If you only want to see the cave, you can also stay at a cheaper place in Santa Fe or Bantayan town.

The resort restaurant is listed as serving from morning to evening, with the hours split into set periods. Between island stops, many visitors eat seafood and Filipino home cooking at restaurants in Santa Fe town or near the port. Menus and prices differ by place.
Check-in is listed as
and check-out as

, and pets are not allowed. Guests of Santa Fe Beach Club, run by the same owner, are reported to get free day use. If you are staying on Bantayan for a while, the least hassle is to pick your island lodging first and then drop in on Ogtong for an hour or two.
Entrance policies and opening hours differ by source, so confirm with the resort's official information or by phone before you leave.
The entrance steps are slippery, so non-slip aqua shoes are safer than sandals.
Bring swimwear, a towel and a waterproof phone case so you can get into the water right away.
Avoid the lunchtime rush and go early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
The entrance fee includes the beach and pool, so it is not a waste if you plan the visit as a half-day rest.
If you have a lot of luggage, leave it at your accommodation and travel light.
Many people rent motorbikes to get around the island, but if you are not confident riding, a tricycle is safer.
Steps are even more slippery on rainy days, so do not push it and change your plans instead.
The depth of the water and the condition of the floor have not been confirmed, and the floor can be slippery. Always keep children under an adult's watch.
The entrance steps are very slippery with moisture. Go down slowly and carefully.
The water level can change with the tides, so the cave looks different depending on when you visit.
When tour groups arrive, queues can form and it can be hard to stay long in the cave.
Young children may be restricted from the cave pool. Follow the staff's instructions on site.
Boats can be cancelled in typhoons or bad weather. Check the latest notices at Hagnaya and Santa Fe ports.
The 2025 earthquake damaged the church in Bantayan town, and entry has been restricted at times. This is separate from a cave visit, but check it when planning other stops on the island.
The whole island that holds the cave, known for white-sand beaches, island tours and island hopping. It is
10 minutes
from Santa Fe Port.
A diving island reached by boat from the northern tip of Cebu. You can combine it with a northern Cebu itinerary.
A group of islands off northeastern Cebu with caves and beaches. It is better to plan it separately from Bantayan.
To reach Hagnaya you pass through Cebu City, where the North Bus Terminal is. It is a good place to look around before you set out.
